Suspected Overdose or Toxidrome

anticholinergic · stimulant · serotonin syndrome · neuroleptic malignant syndrome · lithium · opioid and sedative · cholinergic · salicylate and acetaminophenWhich toxidrome, and what must be checked in every overdose?

Practice
  1. 28-year-old woman on fluoxetine, started tramadol for back pain yesterday agitated, sweating, shivering; clonus at both ankles reflexes brisk; bowel sounds hyperactive; pupils 6 mm T 38.4 °C · HR 122/min → Serotonin syndrome → within a day of adding tramadol to an SSRI, clonus, hyperreflexia, sweating and active bowel sounds mean serotonin syndrome; neuroleptic malignant syndrome brings lead-pipe rigidity over days on a dopamine blocker, and anticholinergic skin is dry
  2. 17-year-old girl took a handful of her mother's pills 2 hours ago alert, oriented; says she wanted to die pupils, skin and bowel sounds normal ECG normal · glucose 96 mg/dL · urine screen negative → Serum acetaminophen level → an intentional ingestion needs an acetaminophen level even when the exam is normal, because early acetaminophen poisoning is often silent and the antidote prevents delayed liver injury; suicide risk is assessed once she is medically clear
  3. 33-year-old man found unresponsive in a public restroom by a friend pupils pinpoint; shallow, slow breaths; groans to a sternal rub needle marks on both forearms; no head injury seen RR 6/min · SpO2 84% · glucose 110 mg/dL → Intravenous naloxone → pinpoint pupils with slow breathing mean opioid toxicity: assisted ventilation and naloxone first, with intubation only if there is no quick response; a benzodiazepine overdose leaves the pupils normal
  4. 46-year-old farmer brought in an hour after spraying his crops vomiting, drooling, tearing; wheezing on both sides pupils 1 mm; bowel sounds hyperactive; diffuse sweating; muscle twitching HR 48/min · BP 98/60 mm Hg → Organophosphate poisoning → pinpoint pupils with secretions everywhere, wheezing and bradycardia after crop spraying mean cholinergic poisoning from an organophosphate; an opioid leaves the patient dry, and anticholinergic toxicity has big pupils and dry skin
  5. 38-year-old woman took an unknown number of pills after an argument ringing in both ears; nausea, vomiting breathing fast and deep; mildly confused T 38.3 °C · RR 30/min · pupils 4 mm → Salicylate poisoning → fever, tinnitus and fast breathing after an overdose point to aspirin, with respiratory alkalosis early and metabolic acidosis later; a salicylate level confirms it
  6. 22-year-old man swallowed 30 sertraline tablets 3 hours ago drowsy, confused; answers slowly no clonus; reflexes normal; pupils 5 mm HR 104/min · BP 118/76 mm Hg · ECG: QRS 92 ms → Levels of common coingestants → an SSRI overdose alone is usually well tolerated, so confusion means another substance: check coingestant levels such as salicylate and ethanol; cyproheptadine is for refractory serotonin syndrome, which this is not
Pairs with Anticholinergic and Tricyclic Toxicity: QRS width, bicarbonate, no physostigmine with a tricyclic. SSRI Adverse Effects: serotonin syndrome. Antipsychotic Adverse Effects: neuroleptic malignant syndrome. Lithium Therapy: toxicity and dialysis. Substance Intoxication and Withdrawal: illicit drugs and alcohol.
Transferable rule

In a suspected overdose, stabilize breathing, glucose and the heart, check acetaminophen and salicylate levels, then let the pupils, skin, bowel sounds and tone name the toxidrome.
